post.summary: Publish an artifact as a new release
post.description: Publishes artifactId (an uploaded bundle, or what a build produced) as a new deployment of serviceId and answers 202 with the deployment and the operation to follow. Refused while the workspace has no current plan (402 PAYMENT_REQUIRED), has an unpaid usage charge (402 PAYMENT_OVERDUE), or is at the spending cap where deploys stop (402 SPENDING_CAP_REACHED); in build mode, at its limit for builds (402 BUILD_LIMIT_REACHED) or for Production (402 BUILD_MODE_GO_LIVE_REQUIRED); or once MDRN stopped the workspace (403 WORKSPACE_BLOCKED). An interrupted publication resumes on its own; repeating the request with the same Idempotency-Key answers the same deployment. A bundle that carries migrations has them applied before anything is published, SQLite's set to the environment's SQLite database and then Postgres' to its Postgres database, each file as one transaction; a failing file fails the deployment with MIGRATION_FAILED, the files before it stay applied, and the previous release keeps serving. Files for a database that is off for the project fail it the same way, with nothing applied to that database. A Postgres database not made yet is made by its first migrations; the deployment waits for it. A bundle the runtime refuses for something in it (a module it imports that is not there, too much CPU while starting, its size, an unknown runtime flag, no handler, an exception at startup) fails the deployment at once with RELEASE_REFUSED, without retrying, and its log says what to change; the previous release keeps serving. Any earlier artifact of the service that is still kept can be published again as a new release, which is how you roll back; it answers 409 CONFLICT when the database already has migrations that artifact does not include. The newest ten releases of a service keep their bundle (three in build mode), and a bundle never released is kept for a week after it was last uploaded or built; an older one answers 409 CONFLICT until it is uploaded or built again.
post.x-mdrn-notes: The deployment and idempotency receipt are durable before acceptance. Each migration file is recorded in the database's own ledger.

post.description: Queues one transactional message and answers 202 with its id in state queued: MDRN has stored it and sends it in the background, so read the message afterwards, or listen to the delivery webhook, for what became of it. The body is either the content itself (subject and text, with html beside it if you want) or a template of the environment (templateId; templates take no variables, so only recipient, attachments and senderId go with it). The sender is a verified domain of the workspace: senderId names one, and without it the workspace's one verified domain is used; 422 SENDER_REQUIRED when the workspace has none or has several and none was named, 409 SENDER_NOT_READY when senderId names a domain that is not verified. App mail never leaves from MDRN's own address. Without a verified sender domain a message goes only to members of your workspace, from MDRN's separate build sender (in build mode named as a build-mode test of your app); anyone else is refused (403 BUILD_MAIL_RECIPIENT in build mode, 422 SENDER_REQUIRED once live). Attachments total at most 256 KiB decoded (four files at most), and the request body at most 425,000 bytes; a larger body is 413 BODY_TOO_LARGE. The same Idempotency-Key answers the same message and sends nothing twice. Marketing, newsletters and campaign messages are not permitted. A message body is kept only until the message is sent or given up and its recipient address for 30 days; a finished message is deleted 90 days after it was accepted.

**Caller:** An app's backend, on its own origin, through Proxy. **Credential:** The release's product credential (mail:send).

Queues one transactional message and answers 202 with its id in state queued; acceptance is not delivery, and the message's state is read afterwards. The body is inline content (subject, text and html if wanted) or a template of the project and environment (templateId; templates take no variables, so only recipient, attachments and senderId go with it). The sender is a verified domain of the workspace: senderId names one, and without it the workspace's one verified domain is used; 422 SENDER_REQUIRED when the workspace has none or several and none was named, 409 SENDER_NOT_READY when senderId names a domain that is not verified. App mail never leaves from MDRN's address. Without a verified sender domain a message goes only to members of your workspace, from MDRN's separate build sender (in build mode named as a build-mode test of your app); anyone else is refused (403 BUILD_MAIL_RECIPIENT in build mode, 422 SENDER_REQUIRED once live). Attachments total at most 256 KiB decoded (four files at most), and the request body at most 425,000 bytes; a larger body returns 413 BODY_TOO_LARGE. Marketing, newsletters and campaign messages are not permitted.

**Scopes:** mail:send.

A message body is kept only until the message is sent or given up and its recipient address for 30 days; a finished message is deleted 90 days after it was accepted. Mail activity is informational: recipient, status and failure details, without message bodies. Delivery webhooks notify the app's backend of status changes; a failed webhook never resends the email.

put.summary: Connect a repository and branch to a service
put.description: Connects serviceId to repositoryId in installationId, on branch or the repository's default branch, and builds what the branch holds now; from then on every push to the branch builds the commit at its head and, when the build succeeds, releases it. Only a repository the installation lists (one you could read when you authorized) can be connected; any other answers 404 NOT_FOUND. A branch with no commit yet, or a repository GitHub refuses MDRN, is not retried: the connection's problem says so until a later push or a reconnect clears it. The repository is held by its numeric identifier, so renaming it does not break the connection. One service deploys one repository and one branch; connecting another replaces the connection. One repository may feed several services, and a push builds each of them.

get.summary: Search the project environment’s application logs
get.description: Searches the logs of every service in the environment, or of one with service, newest first, in the window from and to name (the last hour when omitted). Requests, responses and exceptions are always returned; console lines below the capture level are not. level selects console lines and exceptions by level, as a comma-separated list of debug, log, info, warn and error (anything else answers 400); requests are returned whatever it is. q is at most 256 characters and matches text, without regard to case, in the items as they are answered, redacted and without anything a search leaves out, so it never matches a captured header. It is matched against the text a person reads, as it was written rather than as JSON escapes it: the message, the data logged beside it (its values, at any depth), the path, the service name, the request, invocation, correlation and trace IDs, numbers logged in the data (except under a name for a time: t, ts, or one holding time or date, or ending in At or _at) and the response status; never a field name, any other number, the kind, the level or the cursor. A page searched for text can hold fewer than 100 items while nextCursor goes on. Data logged beside a message is returned with it. Messages, paths and data are redacted: credential-named fields, bearer and basic credentials, cookie headers, credential-named key=value pairs and JSON members, and JSON Web Tokens. Every search reads the project archive, up to the retention setting. It is complete: every request, and every line printed at or above the capture level. An item is usually there within a few minutes of the request. A page holds at most 100 items. Pages walk the archive newest object first: each page is newest first, and an object holds a few minutes of invocations, so neighbouring pages can overlap in time by that much. A walk is bound to its search (from and to as sent, level, q, service) and to the capture level and retention its first page read: a cursor sent with anything else, or after either setting changed, answers 400, and the search starts again without it, so a changed setting never makes a walk pass items over or show them twice. The window’s start as retention clamped it is carried in the cursor, so it does not move with the clock while the walk goes on. Once Logs is deleted for the environment, searches answer 403 PRODUCT_DISABLED until it is enabled again; a disabled Logs stays searchable until what it kept ages out. Every search counts as a read in Logs usage, in the UTC hour it ran. A live tail follows without polling: a first page (sent without cursor) answers tail, where the archive stands; GET /v1/deploy/live sends {kind:"logs",seq} once for each object archived for the environment; reading with tail then answers what was archived past it, at most 100 items (a request is never split, so its own few can pass that), 20 objects or 8 MB, with more true when a bound stopped it, and the next tail. An item has the same cursor from a search and from a tail, so one both answer is one item. After reconnecting, read once from the last tail. A tail read counts as a read like any search.
get.x-mdrn-implementation-status: implemented

post.summary: Switch sign-in on for an app address
post.description: Switches sign-in on for one app address (origin) of the environment, so MDRN serves the sign-in pages there and tells your backend who is signed in. Workspace Admins only, with a credential that reaches the environment, and Auth must be on for the environment (409 PRODUCT_DISABLED). MDRN must already serve an active release of this project and environment at the address: an address MDRN does not serve is 404, one of another project, workspace or environment, or an inactive release, is 403. The answer is 200 with the activation once it succeeded, or with the failed operation; 202 with the unfinished operation otherwise (follow it at Location). The same Idempotency-Key with the same origin, project and environment answers the same operation; other input under it is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. While the operation is retried, your credential, the Admin membership and the address's ownership are checked again.

No session, token or sign-in code is included, and no metadata: user_metadata and app_metadata are kept in the environment's database, in the `_mdrn_metadata` table by user id. While there are more users, the MDRN-Next-Cursor header names the cursor of the next page; ask again with it until the header is absent. The export works whether Auth is on or off, and while the workspace is unpaid, suspended or archived. Requires auth:read, the Admin or Developer role (a Viewer is refused with 403 FORBIDDEN) and current access to the project and environment. Not charged.

post.summary: Get a link that opens an owner-only app
post.description: In build mode an app is served to its owner only: everyone else gets 403 NOT_LIVE_YET. This answers a link that opens the app in a browser for 15 minutes; opening it keeps that browser signed in to the app for 8 hours. lastSeenAt.description: When one of those sessions was last used, in Unix seconds.

enabled.description: Whether the user has two-factor authentication on.

enrolledAt.description: When they turned it on, in Unix seconds; null while it is off.

identities.description: Every way the user signs in, by provider name (email, google or github) and the subject that provider knows the user by: the email address, Google's subject ID or GitHub's user ID. Use them to link Google and GitHub accounts to the same users in another system.

requestId.description: MDRN's id for the request that started the operation. Quote it to support.

attempts.description: How many times MDRN has tried the operation so far; MDRN retries on its own.

progress.description: The step an unfinished operation is on.

lastProblem.description: What interrupted the last attempt of an unfinished operation; MDRN retries it without anyone's help.

origin.description: The app's https address exactly: no path, port, credentials or trailing slash. MDRN must already serve an active release of this project and environment there.

local.description: The part before the @ its mail leaves from: 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit, never two dots in a row. noreply until chosen.
The part before the @ its mail leaves from: 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit, never two dots in a row. noreply until chosen.

address.description: The address its mail leaves from: local@domain.

kind.description: invocation: the request or event itself. log: a line the application printed. exception: an uncaught error.

invocationId.description: The invocation this item belongs to.

correlationId.description: The trace ID MDRN gives a request when it enters (x-mdrn-trace-id), shared by every item of it. Null on items archived before 2026-10-21, which group by requestId.

path.description: The request path; the query string is never kept.

data.description: What the application logged beside the message, bounded; for a message that is a JSON object, its fields.

stack.description: Not returned: the delivered record of an exception holds its name and message only. Kept in the schema for older clients.

deploymentId.description: The release published to carry the change, or null when nothing was serving yet.

value.description: At most 5 KiB. The variables available during build may take at most 64 KiB together, measured as the build receives them (one JSON object, each control character escaped); more answers 400 INVALID_REQUEST and nothing is set.

secret.description: A plain variable is stored encrypted the same way; this records whether it is treated as a secret. A secret's value is never returned; a plain one is listed back.

build.description: Also give it to every build of the service, secret or not, as an environment variable of the build steps. Never printed or stored with the build.

problem.description: Why the connection does not build: GitHub has no commit on the branch yet, refused MDRN the repository, the GitHub App was uninstalled or suspended, or the repository was taken out of what MDRN may see. Null while nothing is wrong; cleared once a build of the connection starts or it is connected again.

migrations.description: mdrn.jsonc's "migrations": a directory per database, relative to rootDirectory. The string form of a bundle built before still reads.

schedules.description: Paths MDRN calls on a timetable while this release is the active one.

name.description: The schedule’s name, kept across releases: a release that keeps a name keeps its history and next fire.

cron.description: Five fields, or @hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly or @yearly, in UTC. When day of month and day of week are both restricted, a day matching either fires; a field starting with * (such as */2) counts as unrestricted for that rule, as in Vixie cron. Runs of one schedule are not kept apart: an app still working after its attempt timed out, or a retry, can overlap the next fire.

path.description: An absolute path in this app; MDRN sends a POST to it.

config.description: mdrn.jsonc as this build resolved it; null until the build has run.

prebuilt.description: An uploaded build (mdrn deploy --prebuilt): built elsewhere with mdrn build, checked and released without a build machine. The time that takes counts in container minutes like any build.

migrationState.description: none: the release brought no migrations. up_to_date: every file was already applied. applied: this deployment applied at least one. failed: migration processing was refused. Earlier files may remain applied; inspect migrationOutcome, migrationsApplied and migrationWarnings.

migrationOutcome.description: What this release did to the database, kept across retries and whether or not the code was published.

migrationsApplied.description: Each migration file this deployment applied, named with its database first (sqlite/ or postgres/, then the file). A deployment made before files named their database lists bare names.

migrationFailed.description: The file that failed, named with its database.

startedBy.description: Who started it: a member of the workspace (accountId; the console names them as the team list does), a workspace token (name), or a push from GitHub (name, the pusher's GitHub login). A rollback, a retry and Copy to Production name whoever asked for them. Null when it was started before this was recorded, or by something that names nobody, such as a variable change.

containerSeconds.description: The container time this build counts, in seconds: from when it started on the builder until it ended, as the Container minutes line of the bill adds it up. Null until it has started and ended.

artifactPrunedAt.description: In the build list: when the bundle of this build was removed, so deploying its artifact again answers 409; null while it is kept.

limit.description: The most build mode allows of the line in total while in build mode, counted since the workspace was created, in the meter’s own unit; per database where the line is per database.

stops.description: What stops when the line reaches its limit.

limits.description: Build mode’s limit on each capped tariff line, by meter.

used.description: What build mode used of each capped line in total since the workspace was created, by meter, as last rated; a per-database line shows its largest database.

reached.description: The meters at their limit: what they stop answers 402 BUILD_LIMIT_REACHED until the workspace goes live: a used-up limit stays used up.

build.description: Build mode, the free way to start with no card: its caps and what it used of them. Null once the workspace has gone live on the plan, or when it lapsed after a payment.

liveAt.description: Unix seconds: when the workspace went live, its first plan payment’s period start. Null before it goes live.

capChosen.description: Whether an Admin chose a spending cap (no cap included) since going live, as the go-live screens ask; workspaces live before this existed count as having chosen.

until.description: Unix seconds: the end of the 14 days to withdraw.

consumer.description: True for a consumer in the EU (a billing address in one of its 27 member states and no tax ID); null while not known.

country.description: The billing address’s country, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, when known.

withdrawal.description: While the workspace may withdraw from its first plan in Billing, within 14 days of going live, for an EU consumer or a customer not known yet to be one (so an EU consumer never misses it); null otherwise, and null for a customer known not to be an EU consumer. An Admin withdraws with POST …/billing/withdrawal; a UK consumer, or anyone, writes to support.

provider.description: The stage’s billing mode (BILLING_PROVIDER): sandbox, stripe_test or stripe_live; null where none is set.

planProvider.description: Who wrote the workspace’s plan: manual when MDRN granted it by hand, otherwise the billing mode it was bought through (sandbox, stripe_test or stripe_live). Null when the workspace has no plan row.

endsAt.description: Unix seconds: when a plan its customer cancelled in the billing portal ends. It stays current and grants everything until then, and is not renewed; resuming it in the portal clears this. Null while the plan renews, and once it is no longer current.

creditCents.description: Prepaid credit balance in US cents, before tax. Usage beyond the plan is paid from it first when a billing period closes.

pricedUsage.description: Whether usage beyond the plan is charged on this stage when a billing period closes.

active.description: Whether the workspace has a current plan; without one its apps are not served.

enabled.description: Whether threshold invoicing runs on this stage.

thresholdCents.description: When unbilled usage beyond the plan reaches this many US cents, it is charged at once: 2500 for every workspace. After a failed payment, the same amount of new unbilled usage refuses service where suspension is on.

unbilledCents.description: Usage beyond the plan this period not yet billed, after prepaid credit, as last rated.

paymentFailed.description: A threshold invoice is unpaid after a failed payment.

suspended.description: Apps, builds and product calls are refused until the unpaid threshold invoice is paid.

payUrl.description: The payment page for the unpaid threshold invoice: the console’s “Pay and restore”. Paying it restores an archived workspace automatically.

reason.description: Why it is archived: an unpaid usage charge (paying it restores), or a plan no longer current, cancelled or unpaid past its 3 days (buying a plan restores).

since.description: Unix seconds: when the workspace was suspended and archiving began.

deleteAt.description: Unix seconds: everything still archived is deleted then, 90 days after since.

limitCents.description: What keeping the archive may cost MDRN, in US cents: 1000.

costCents.description: What keeping what is still archived has cost MDRN so far, in US cents.

state.description: live: kept in its own database (SQLite over 5 GB, Postgres), refused while suspended.

parked.description: The move did not finish within a day and is no longer retried on its own: MDRN has been told and sends it again.

archive.description: A workspace suspended for non-payment, or whose plan is no longer current, has its SQLite, Postgres and Objects data archived, kept 90 days and up to $10 of MDRN’s cost, and restored when paid. Null when nothing is archived.

capCents.description: Stop when usage beyond what the plan includes reaches this amount this month, in US cents; null for no limit, the default.

alertCents.description: Email the Admins, once a month, when usage beyond what the plan includes reaches this amount, in US cents; null for no email.

atCap.description: What stops at the cap, product by product, as the Admin chose; keepRunning unless chosen.

spentCents.description: This period’s estimate of usage beyond the plan, in US cents: the lines that could be measured, so a lower bound when a line is unavailable.

checkedAt.description: Unix seconds when the estimate was last rated.

warning.description: spentCents has reached alertCents; false with no alert.

enforced.description: Whether reaching the cap stops the products chosen in atCap on this stage; elsewhere it is shown only.

chosenAt.description: Unix seconds: when an Admin last chose the cap (no cap included); null if never.

suspended.description: Whether the workspace is suspended over a disputed payment, its own or one an Admin of it made: apps, builds, schedules and product calls stop and the console takes no changes until MDRN lifts it. Nothing is deleted.

observedAt.description: Unix seconds when this usage view was read; individual meters may arrive later.

meterWindow.description: Earliest and latest event time of the meters, across all recorded history.

logsUsage.description: What Logs used over the period under view (the named period, else the trailing thirty days): average GB stored, byte-seconds stored, bytes and objects written to the archive, log lines, searches and bytes they read. Shown as usage and never in the ledger; log lines are charged through the tariff (see charges). complete=false with no meters when Logs does not answer.

charging.description: Whether closed periods are charged on this stage.

creditCents.description: Prepaid credit left, in US cents.

estimate.description: Usage beyond the plan for the current billing period so far, rated against the tariff. complete=false when any source did not answer; such a line has no quantity.

included.description: Units included each period, in the meter unit.

microUsd.description: Price in micro-USD for every `per` units beyond the included ones.

perDatabase.description: Included per database rather than per workspace.

projects.description: The quantity per project, largest first, where the line’s source splits it by project; absent for a line measured for the whole workspace only (custom domains, build time).

name.description: null for a project since deleted.

unattributed.description: With projects: the part of quantity no project could be named for.

series.description: One point per UTC day of the period so far: the quantity of the project named by projectId when the line splits by project, else of the whole workspace, with each project’s share. Days add up to the quantity, except for custom domains, whose points are each closed day’s domains beyond the included ones and whose quantity is the highest of them.

day.description: Start of the UTC day, unix seconds.

projects.description: Without projectId: each project’s share of the day; the rest is unattributed.

workspace.description: With projectId, on a line split by project: every project’s quantity that day, which is what the included amount is held against.

services.description: On lines that carry services: each service’s share of the day, in the same scope; the rest names no service.

The quantity per service (deployment), largest first, of the project named by projectId, else of every project; only on lines whose source names the service: Requests and CPU time from our network’s analytics, and build time. Objects gateway and Database requests on the Requests line name no service. On Postgres compute and storage, Auth’s share is the one service, serviceId auth, named Auth, with an empty environment; the rest is the databases’, and the field is absent where no Auth counts on the line. Absent on other lines measured per project only (Database, Objects, Mail, log lines) or per workspace (custom domains).

closed.description: The closed period named by periodId, else the latest: what each meter charged, from prepaid credit and on the invoice.

thresholdCents.description: Cents of this line a threshold invoice already billed during the period.

quantity.description: Null while a measurement is unknown.

use.description: deployment: the host serves serviceId. downloads: the host serves the environment's Objects download links, and an app's download links name it once it is active.

serviceId.description: The service the host serves; null for a downloads host.

ownedDomainId.description: The domain of this environment the host sits under (GET /v1/deploy/owned-domains), when there is one.

state.description: ownership_pending: waiting for the DNS records below. ssl_pending: ownership is proven and the certificate is being issued. active: serving. failed: our network refused or gave up; error says why. deleting: out of traffic, being removed from our network.

optional.description: The routing CNAME is required, and so is MDRN's ownership TXT (_mdrn-challenge.<hostname>) until the workspace has proved the hostname is its own: our network's verification is believed only once that record has been seen. Our network's own ownership TXT is optional, for moving a live site without downtime.

charge.description: The price accepted when the hostname was added beyond the included ones; null for an included hostname.

checkedAt.description: When MDRN last asked our network where the hostname stands (unix seconds); null before the first check. POST .../verify within 5 minutes of it answers that check.

included.description: Hostnames included per workspace, across every project and environment.

microUsdPerMonth.description: Price of each hostname beyond the included ones.

text.description: The plain-text body, at most 32 KiB.

html.description: An HTML body, at most 32 KiB, sent beside the plain-text one.

templateId.description: A template of the project and environment, which supplies subject, text and html. Templates take no variables.

attachments.description: At most four files, 256 KiB decoded in all.

filename.description: No path separators or control characters, and ends in the extension of its type: .pdf, .png, .jpg or .jpeg, and .txt, .csv or .log for text/plain.

senderId.description: A verified sender domain of the workspace. Omit it when the workspace has exactly one.

MessageInput.description: One transactional message: inline content (subject and text, with html if wanted) or a template (templateId, with which only recipient, attachments and senderId are allowed). The sender is a verified domain of the workspace, never a shared MDRN address.

requestId.description: The request's id; quote it when you write to support.

QueuedMessage.description: The accepted message: its id and state queued. MDRN has stored it and sends it in the background; read the message for what became of it.

migrationState.description: none: the release brought no migrations. up_to_date: every file was already applied. applied: this deployment applied at least one. failed: migration processing was refused. Earlier files may remain applied; inspect migrationOutcome, migrationsApplied and migrationWarnings.

migrationsApplied.description: Each migration file this deployment applied, named with its database first (sqlite/ or postgres/, then the file). A deployment made before files named their database lists bare names.

migrationOutcome.description: What this release did to the database, kept across retries and whether or not the code was published.

migrationFailed.description: The file that failed, named with its database.

startedBy.description: Who started it: a member of the workspace (accountId; the console names them as the team list does), a workspace token (name), or a push from GitHub (name, the pusher's GitHub login). A rollback, a retry and Copy to Production name whoever asked for them. Null when it was started before this was recorded, or by something that names nobody, such as a variable change.

lifecycleTiming.description: When each event of the deployment was observed, in Unix milliseconds, for diagnosis. An event that was not observed is absent. These include waits for scheduling and are not part of the stage durations in releaseTiming.

productionEnvironmentId.description: The id of its Production environment.

secondFactorRequired.description: Whether its Admins require two-factor authentication of every member: a member without it reads, and every change they make in it is refused (403 SECOND_FACTOR_REQUIRED) until they turn it on.
